specificationPolicy.legacyReference: ISO 32000-1:2008 and the earlier Adobe PDF versions
specificationPolicy.defaultOutput: Preserve the input's declared PDF version where safely possible; emit PDF 2.0 when the selected workflow requires it or PDFE cannot safely author the earlier-version form.
outputRules: Do not emit a PDF 2.0-only feature without upgrading the declared version and testing both the new feature and preservation of unrelated content.
Do not downgrade, preserve a version declaration, or claim a conformance profile when the changed output cannot safely satisfy that declaration or claim.
Do not write features deprecated by PDF 2.0; legacy files may still need parse/preserve handling.
Do not call a feature supported merely because it parses or round-trips; support is mode-specific.

redactionReviewDrafts.purpose: Explicit, internal review of proposed redactions before destructive content removal.
redactionReviewDrafts.ordinarySave: Preserve incoming /Redact annotations without applying them.
redactionReviewDrafts.reviewDraftSave: When explicitly enabled, write /Redact annotations and a clear non-shareable warning; no security-removal claim is permitted.
redactionReviewDrafts.safeRedactedCopy: Never create /Redact annotations. Refuse to produce a safe-redacted copy with unresolved incoming /Redact annotations rather than silently applying or deleting them.
redactionReviewDrafts.application: Applying an explicitly reviewed annotation must remove the identified content, draw any post-removal overlay as page content, and delete the applied annotation.

editingSafetyPolicy.unsupportedOrAmbiguousFeature: A document may be viewed in clearly limited mode, but PDFE refuses editing or redaction when it cannot safely render or mutate a relevant feature and explains the reason on the attempted action.
editingSafetyPolicy.malformedOrDamagedDocument: Offer clearly marked best-effort read-only recovery only; refuse editing, redaction, and conformance claims until parsing is safe and deterministic.
editingSafetyPolicy.saveStrategy: Default to a full normalized rewrite after editing. Incremental-save workflows are deferred unless separately justified.
editingSafetyPolicy.resourceLimits: Define maximum file, object, nesting, decoded-stream, image-pixel, and rendering budgets; reject over-limit inputs safely with an explanation.

conformancePolicy.marketing: Do not claim blanket PDF 2.0 conformance. Publish the evidence-backed capability profile instead.
conformancePolicy.profiles: After an edit, remove PDF/A, PDF/UA, PDF/X, PDF/E, or PDF/VT conformance claims unless PDFE independently verifies that the output remains conforming.
conformancePolicy.formalClaims: Make formal profile claims only in specific independently validated output modes.

evidencePolicy.higherConfidence: Redistributable real-world corpus coverage raises confidence above implemented.
evidencePolicy.securitySensitive: Require independent saved-file and rendered-output checks before calling a security-sensitive capability implemented.
evidencePolicy.benchmarkScope: Benchmarks are required for open, render, search, save, redact, and forms; record a stated metric and threshold where applicable.
evidencePolicy.redactionReleaseRule: A confirmed redaction leak blocks release only when it is a regression. A newly discovered pre-existing leak is a priority remediation item with recorded scope and owner.
evidencePolicy.corpusPrivacy: Use only redistributable public or official fixtures and anonymized synthetic material. Never upload private documents; run reference tools locally and record tool, version, command, and claim.

activeContentPolicy.https: Only a deliberate user click may launch an https URI in the system browser. Show the normalized destination and permit a user-managed trusted-host allowlist that no PDF can modify.
activeContentPolicy.http: Never follow insecure http. Explain the risk and offer copy/inspection or an https alternative.
activeContentPolicy.mailto: Require confirmation showing recipient, subject, and body before opening the mail client.
activeContentPolicy.otherSchemes: Block and allow copy-only for all other URI schemes, including local, executable, custom-app, data, and script schemes.
activeContentPolicy.otherActions: Never automatically execute actions. Block JavaScript, Launch, remote-document, embedded-document, multimedia, form-submit, and external-data execution.

priorityCapabilities: safe parsing, bounded decoding, and conservative round-trip preservation
page viewing, rendering, search, selection, copy, and common font/image content
content-level redaction with independent saved-byte, extraction, and visual evidence
page organization and ordinary document editing
mainstream AcroForms (fill, save, flatten) and everyday annotations
metadata, embedded files, encryption, permissions, and signature inspection
reliable viewing, search, selection, and redaction for complex writing systems
selectedPdf20Capabilities: associated files and current embedded-file semantics
PDF 2.0 header/catalog acceptance and current errata-based interpretation
tagged-PDF namespace-aware preservation before any claim of semantic authoring
preserveOnlyOrDeferred: XFA and deprecated form presentation behavior
rich media, movie, sound, 3D, PRC, and projection
geospatial, measurement, document-part, and print-production workflows
PDF/A, PDF/UA, PDF/X, PDF/E, and PDF/VT conformance claims
full accessibility repair or authoring beyond evidence-backed workflows

adoptionEvidence.note: PDF does not require implementation of every feature; implemented features must be correct.
PDF 2.0 supplies corrections and clarifications relevant to PDF 1.7 implementations.
Tagged-PDF data model is shared but PDF 2.0 adds namespace semantics.
